B. How the agents must use the dictionary
Use only data elements listed here. Refer to them by Element ID in every finding (e.g. D007 = 5.6 mEq/L on 2026-09-30, source EHR).
Use only items the patient has confirmed and that are reconciled across sources. Ignore pending or conflicting items and point to the Review screen instead.
If the latest value is older than 'Valid for analysis', treat it as missing. Never use an outdated value as current.
Never assume a missing value is normal. If a rule needs it, say it is missing and suggest a question, e.g. 'When was your last potassium test?'
Always report value, unit and date. Convert units only using the Unit column (e.g. lb to kg).
Each agent works mainly with elements where 'Used by agent' includes its role. Other elements may be read for context but not interpreted outside the agent's discipline.
MVP elements may be requested from the patient. 'Later' elements are used only if already present; never ask the patient for them.
Use the calculated phenotype (D003) based on U.S. definitions. Do not re-derive it.
Red-flag symptoms in D014 and a positive PHQ-9 item 9 in D016 trigger the urgent pathway immediately. Do not wait for analysis.
Never request data that is not in this dictionary. Never diagnose or give dosing instructions; findings end with a question for the clinician.
Every finding cites the Element IDs used and the rule or recommendation card that applies.
Judge values with the Thresholds sheet. Order: (1) clinician's patient-specific target, (2) the lab's reported range, (3) default values. Always state which one was used.
